_doc: bsv-low #474. Prose and the rules of change: docs/STORAGE-OWNERSHIP.md. Checked by scripts/check-storage-ownership.py (make ci). owner = the crate whose statements own the rows (it may issue any statement but the never-wipe rule's); writers = further write grants by crate and op; readers = read grants (an INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / REPLACE grant implies a read, a DDL grant does not); schema_owner may CREATE / ALTER / DROP every table of the shared database (its migrations own the schema). never_wipe = true: no crate, the owner and the schema owner included, may DROP or TRUNCATE the table, ALTER it with DROP COLUMN or RENAME, or DELETE from it with no WHERE; a DELETE with a WHERE only where the row's delete_scope names the crate, the file and the statement (the literal, whitespace collapsed, at most 120 characters). not_tables = words the scanner reads as a table, scoped to one crate and its ops. dynamic_sites = string-built table names, each site named by its statement.

tables.name: ef_deferred_jobs
tables.holds: NL-6c: one row per broadcast-gated submission whose EF work was past one request's budget: its reference (the sha256 of what was submitted), where its bytes rest, its state, its runs, the corroboration's cursor (legs_from, NL-6d) and the arm's answer once a run ended; a settled row is swept by the cron seven days after its last write
tables.why: the deferral's ledger: a lost row loses the caller's poll and the queued run of a submission the network has not been handed; transient, so its sweep needs no delete_scope

tables.name: ef_deferred_chunks
tables.holds: NL-6c: the bytes of a deferred submission at rest in D1, a chunk of at most 1,000,000 bytes a row (under D1's 2,000,000-byte row), when the Worker has no BEEF_BLOBS binding; deleted when the job settles
tables.why: bytes at rest for the queue consumer's run; a lost chunk fails that job's run (the job ends failed, the caller re-presents)

tables.name: gasp_deferred_graphs
tables.holds: the partial walks of GASP graphs deferred past their per-graph budget (bsv-low #555), one row per graph, at most 256 rows and 64 MiB of records over every peer (the upsert's ceiling; `bytes` is a whole record's, its parts in gasp_deferred_graph_chunks included) and swept by the cron 30 h after its last write (the lens fold's M3); a record has no byte bound (bsv-low #585) and the row holds its first 1 MiB
tables.why: a cache of peer requests: a lost row costs the walk again from its root; transient, so its sweep needs no delete_scope (the checker refuses one on a table that is not never-wipe)

tables.name: gasp_deferred_graph_chunks
tables.holds: the further parts of a deferred GASP graph's record past one row's room (bsv-low #585), 1 MiB a row, keyed by the graph, the generation its gasp_deferred_graphs row names and a sequence; written before the head row, deleted with it, and a part no head names is swept by the cron after an hour
tables.why: D1's 2 MB row is routed around, not made a limit on a graph: a lost part drops its record, which costs the walk again from its root; transient

tables.name: beef_blob_sweep
tables.holds: the one-row state of the orphan sweep over the queue's R2 objects (bsv-low #585, door 3's fold): the last key a pass handled, the objects and bytes counted by the round in progress, the last complete round's count, the last pass
tables.why: the cron's sweep lists BEEF_BLOBS 200 objects a pass and resumes from the key at rest; a lost row restarts the round at the first key and loses only the served count until a round completes; transient

tables.name: mutation_dead_letters
tables.holds: the dead-lettered mutation messages (bytes, or since bsv-low #585 door 3 the R2 key of a BEEF past the queue's inline room, in `r2_key` / `r2_bytes`; topics, mode), their last fault, attempts, status, re-drives and park history
tables.why: bsv-low #576: once the DLQ consumer acks a dead letter this row is its only copy, and the operator's lever re-drives from it; the lens fold (M2): a DELETE is the ack of the letter's LANDED bytes (a row then copies nothing); the delta fold (D-M1): the other is the operator's discard of a parked letter by key, so the ceiling can drain; bounded rows (2000 letters with bytes) and bytes per row (one queue message, 20 history entries)

delete_scope.statement: DELETE FROM mutation_dead_letters WHERE txid = ? AND topics = ? RETURNING status, parked_at, r2_key
delete_scope.why: dead_letters::resolve (RESOLVE_SQL): the main consumer acked a replay of this key, so its bytes LANDED (durable, or refused under an open eviction); the row, a failing note or a parked / re-driven letter, is a copy of nothing

delete_scope.statement: DELETE FROM mutation_dead_letters WHERE txid = ?1 AND (?2 IS NULL OR topics = ?2) AND status = 'parked' AND rowid IN (SE
delete_scope.why: dead_letters::internal_discard (DISCARD_SQL, the delta fold D-M1): POST /internal/discard-dead-letters, bearer INTERNAL_TOKEN, the operator discards a named PARKED letter (never a redriven one in flight, never a failing note) to make room under the 2000-letter ceiling, at most 50 keys and (the delta-2 fold, D2-L1) 50 rows per call, oldest parked first, each logged DISCARDED with the sha256 of its bytes and counted dead_letters_discarded_total
